content:
Earlier this July, Apple added basic search functionality to its TestFlight app. You might think such a simple update would be widely welcomed, but the same TestFlight update introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I was not significantly affected by this bug. Precisely because of that, I initially thought the TestFlight update was a simple yet meaningful improvement.

Sometimes a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large number of beta apps, as seen with Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 adds a "search bar for quickly searching apps".

Looking back, I did notice some oddities, which I have noted at the bottom of the article (though my understanding at the time was completely the reverse):

I think the reason I did not realise this was a bug is that I have been keeping TestFlight beta apps from over the years in order to "merge" what were originally separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts. It is not the most convenient arrangement, but for me it is worthwhile.

In any case, the TestFlight bug did not escape the attention of John Vorhees at MacStories:

So, when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac about TestFlight adding a search bar, you can imagine how excited I was. I thought to myself, "Finally!" I immediately put down what I was doing and updated the app. [...] Unfortunately, there is a big "but" to this story. In the past, TestFlight beta versions were listed in reverse chronological order, which I personally liked very much. [...] Now, those expired beta versions are mixed in alphabetically with currently active TestFlight betas, and the expired beta list seems to have expanded to include every beta I have ever participated in. I did a quick count, and for me it came to around 800 app entries. As you can imagine, very few of these are actually active betas. The search function does help, but scrolling through is no longer a viable way to find things.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote about the TestFlight update and the bug on Daring Fireball:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was pointed out by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the release notes only mention bug fixes, this update did in fact fix the bug in question.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is a fix for users affected by this regression issue.
